rows.title: Day 1
rows.raw: Isaiah opens by exposing Judah's rebellion, empty worship, social injustice, and the Lord's call to cleansing and repentance.

rows.title: Day 2
rows.raw: Isaiah sees the Lord's holiness, is cleansed, and is sent into a hard ministry amid judgment and promise.

rows.title: Day 3
rows.raw: Isaiah promises a Spirit-filled ruler from Jesse's line, then turns to songs of salvation and oracles over the nations.

rows.title: Day 4
rows.raw: Isaiah speaks oracles concerning Moab, Damascus, Cush, and Egypt, showing the Lord's authority over all nations.

rows.title: Day 5
rows.raw: Isaiah gives signs and oracles against nations and cities that trust power, wealth, alliances, or reputation.

rows.title: Day 6
rows.raw: Isaiah widens the view to worldwide judgment, songs of trust, and the Lord's promised feast where death is swallowed up.

rows.title: Day 7
rows.raw: Isaiah confronts pride, false refuge, empty counsel, and reliance on Egypt rather than quiet trust in the Lord.

rows.title: Day 8
rows.raw: Isaiah looks toward righteous rule, the Spirit poured out, judgment on evil, and restoration pictured as a blossoming wilderness.

rows.title: Day 9
rows.raw: Jerusalem faces Assyrian intimidation, Hezekiah prays, the Lord delivers, and later Hezekiah stumbles through pride.

rows.title: Day 10
rows.raw: Isaiah announces comfort, the greatness of God, the servant of the Lord, and redemption through waters and fire.

rows.title: Day 11
rows.raw: Isaiah contrasts the living Lord with powerless idols and announces God's sovereign purpose through Cyrus.

rows.title: Day 12
rows.raw: The Lord confronts stubbornness, calls His people to listen, and reveals His servant as light to the nations.

rows.title: Day 13
rows.raw: Isaiah announces good news, describes the suffering Servant, and invites the thirsty to come and receive mercy.

rows.title: Day 14
rows.raw: Isaiah speaks of welcome for outsiders, true fasting, justice, sin, and the Lord's own arm bringing salvation.

rows.title: Day 15
rows.raw: Isaiah looks toward Zion's glory, the anointed messenger of good news, and the Lord's final victory.

rows.title: Day 16
rows.raw: Isaiah ends with longing for God to act, warnings of judgment, new creation hope, and Jeremiah begins with a prophet set apart.

rows.title: Day 17
rows.raw: Jeremiah begins by bringing the Lord's covenant case against Judah for forsaking Him and chasing worthless gods.

rows.title: Day 18
rows.raw: Jeremiah warns of coming disaster, shallow healing, rejected correction, and grief over Judah's sin.

rows.title: Day 19
rows.raw: Jeremiah contrasts idols with the living God and uses vivid signs to expose Judah's pride and covenant unfaithfulness.

rows.title: Day 20
rows.raw: Jeremiah laments drought and judgment, warns against false prophecy, and contrasts cursed trust in man with blessed trust in the Lord.

rows.title: Day 21
rows.raw: The Lord sends Jeremiah to the potter's house and continues warning Judah through signs and confrontation.

rows.title: Day 22
rows.raw: Jeremiah confronts kings and leaders, announces judgment, and promises a righteous Branch from David's line.

rows.title: Day 23
rows.raw: Jeremiah faces danger for speaking God's word and later writes to exiles, calling them to seek the welfare of the city.

rows.title: Day 24
rows.raw: These chapters gather promises of restoration, return, healing, Davidic hope, and the new covenant written on the heart.

rows.title: Day 25
rows.raw: Judah's leaders make and break a covenant to free servants, while Jeremiah continues warning amid political pressure.

rows.title: Day 26
rows.raw: Jeremiah is thrown into a cistern, rescued, and later witnesses the fall of Jerusalem and its aftermath.

rows.title: Day 27
rows.raw: The remnant asks Jeremiah to seek the Lord, but they reject the answer and flee toward Egypt.

rows.title: Day 28
rows.raw: Jeremiah speaks oracles against surrounding nations, showing that the Lord's rule extends beyond Judah.

rows.title: Day 29
rows.raw: Jeremiah ends with judgment on Babylon and the fall of Jerusalem, then Lamentations begins with grief over the ruined city.

rows.title: Day 30
rows.raw: Lamentations grieves Jerusalem's destruction, confesses sin, and reaches for hope in the Lord's steadfast love.

rows.title: Day 31
rows.raw: Ezekiel is among the exiles by the Chebar canal when he sees the glory of the Lord and receives a difficult prophetic calling.

rows.title: Day 32
rows.raw: Ezekiel acts out Jerusalem's judgment, prophesies against idolatry, and is shown hidden abominations in the temple.

rows.title: Day 33
rows.raw: Ezekiel sees judgment on Jerusalem, the glory departing, and signs that exile is truly coming.

rows.title: Day 34
rows.raw: The Lord rebukes false prophets, exposes idolatry, and describes Jerusalem's covenant unfaithfulness in painful detail.

rows.title: Day 35
rows.raw: Ezekiel uses parables and history to show Jerusalem's rebellion while holding out the Lord's future promise.

rows.title: Day 36
rows.raw: Ezekiel announces the sword, exposes corrupt leadership and worship, and marks Jerusalem's siege with painful signs.

rows.title: Day 37
rows.raw: The Lord speaks judgment against surrounding nations, especially Tyre, for pride, violence, and rejoicing over Judah's fall.

rows.title: Day 38
rows.raw: Ezekiel announces judgment on Egypt and Pharaoh, using images of monsters, trees, and descent to the grave.

rows.title: Day 39
rows.raw: Ezekiel is renewed as watchman, Israel's shepherds are judged, and the Lord promises cleansing, a new heart, and His Spirit.

rows.title: Day 40
rows.raw: Ezekiel sees dry bones raised, the people reunited under one shepherd, enemies defeated, and a restored temple vision beginning.

rows.title: Day 41
rows.raw: Ezekiel continues the temple vision, sees the Lord's glory return, and hears instructions about holiness and worship.

rows.title: Day 42
rows.raw: Ezekiel's vision concludes with restored worship, renewed land, a life-giving river, and a city named for the Lord's presence.

rows.title: Day 43
rows.raw: Daniel and his friends serve in Babylon while remaining faithful, interpreting dreams, facing the furnace, and seeing a proud king humbled.

rows.title: Day 44
rows.raw: Daniel interprets Babylon's fall, survives the lions' den, and receives visions of kingdoms that rise and pass away.

rows.title: Day 45
rows.raw: Daniel prays confession over Israel's exile and receives visions of conflict, endurance, and final resurrection hope.

rows.title: Day 1
rows.raw: The risen Jesus teaches His apostles, promises the Holy Spirit, ascends, and prepares them for witness.

rows.title: Day 2
rows.raw: At Pentecost, Peter proclaims that God raised Jesus and made Him both Lord and Christ.

rows.title: Day 3
rows.raw: Peter and John meet a lame man at the temple gate, and he is healed in Jesus' name.

rows.title: Day 4
rows.raw: Peter and John testify before leaders after healing a man in Jesus' name.

rows.title: Day 5
rows.raw: Acts 5 includes the judgment of Ananias and Sapphira, signs among the people, opposition, and renewed apostolic witness.

rows.title: Day 6
rows.raw: A practical need in the church leads to Spirit-filled servants being appointed, and Stephen's witness begins.

rows.title: Day 7
rows.raw: Stephen retells Israel's story, exposes resistance to God, and dies while seeing the exalted Christ.

rows.title: Day 8
rows.raw: Persecution scatters believers, Philip preaches in Samaria, and an Ethiopian official receives the gospel.

rows.title: Day 9
rows.raw: Saul persecutes the church until the risen Jesus confronts him on the road to Damascus.

rows.title: Day 10
rows.raw: Peter is sent to Cornelius, and Gentiles receive the Holy Spirit as the gospel crosses another boundary.

rows.title: Day 11
rows.raw: Peter explains Gentile inclusion, and the church in Antioch grows through scattered believers and faithful teaching.

rows.title: Day 12
rows.raw: James is killed, Peter is imprisoned, and the church prays while God delivers Peter.

rows.title: Day 13
rows.raw: The church in Antioch sends Barnabas and Saul, and Paul proclaims Jesus from Israel's story.

rows.title: Day 14
rows.raw: Paul and Barnabas preach, suffer opposition, and strengthen new disciples before returning to Antioch.

rows.title: Day 15
rows.raw: The Jerusalem council addresses whether Gentile believers must take on the law of Moses to be saved.

rows.title: Day 16
rows.raw: Paul's team is led to Macedonia, Lydia believes, a slave girl is freed, and a jailer is saved.

rows.title: Day 17
rows.raw: Paul reasons in synagogues and speaks in Athens, proclaiming the Creator and the risen Judge.

rows.title: Day 18
rows.raw: Paul ministers in Corinth, receives encouragement from the Lord, and later Apollos is taught more accurately.

rows.title: Day 19
rows.raw: In Ephesus, the gospel confronts incomplete understanding, spiritual counterfeits, magic, and economic idolatry.

rows.title: Day 20
rows.raw: Paul encourages believers, raises Eutychus, and gives farewell counsel to the Ephesian elders.

rows.title: Day 21
rows.raw: Paul travels toward Jerusalem despite warnings and is arrested after unrest in the temple.

rows.title: Day 22
rows.raw: Paul tells his conversion story to a hostile crowd in Jerusalem.

rows.title: Day 23
rows.raw: Paul faces division, danger, and a plot against his life, but the Lord stands by him.

rows.title: Day 24
rows.raw: Paul gives his defense before Felix and remains imprisoned while Felix delays justice.

rows.title: Day 25
rows.raw: Paul stands before Festus, appeals to Caesar, and continues moving toward Rome through legal proceedings.

rows.title: Day 26
rows.raw: Paul testifies before Agrippa, retelling his calling and proclaiming Christ's suffering and resurrection.

rows.title: Day 27
rows.raw: Paul sails toward Rome, the ship is caught in a violent storm, and God promises preservation.

rows.title: Day 28
rows.raw: Paul reaches Rome, ministers on Malta, and proclaims the kingdom of God and Jesus Christ under house arrest.

rows.title: Day 1
rows.raw: Romans opens with Paul's eagerness to preach the gospel, then exposes Gentile and Jewish need before God.

rows.title: Day 2
rows.raw: Paul explains that all have sinned and that righteousness comes through faith in Christ, using Abraham as a witness.

rows.title: Day 3
rows.raw: Paul connects justification with peace, hope, union with Christ, and freedom from slavery to sin.

rows.title: Day 4
rows.raw: Paul names the struggle with sin and then announces life, assurance, help, and hope in the Spirit.

rows.title: Day 5
rows.raw: Paul grieves for Israel and reflects on God's mercy, human response, and the nearness of the word of faith.

rows.title: Day 6
rows.raw: Paul moves from God's mercy in His saving purposes to the call to present our bodies as living sacrifices.

rows.title: Day 7
rows.raw: Paul addresses civic responsibility, love as fulfilling the law, and patient welcome among believers with different consciences.

rows.title: Day 8
rows.raw: Paul closes Romans by calling believers to welcome one another, hope in Scripture, and participate in gospel mission.

rows.title: Day 9
rows.raw: Paul addresses a divided church by centering them on the cross and the wisdom revealed by the Spirit.

rows.title: Day 10
rows.raw: Paul confronts spiritual immaturity, leader factions, and pride in the Corinthian church.

rows.title: Day 11
rows.raw: Paul addresses serious sin, church discipline, lawsuits, sexual immorality, and the believer's body as belonging to Christ.

rows.title: Day 12
rows.raw: Paul gives pastoral counsel about marriage, singleness, calling, conscience, and food offered to idols.

rows.title: Day 13
rows.raw: Paul describes surrendering rights for the gospel and warns from Israel's wilderness failures.

rows.title: Day 14
rows.raw: Paul addresses worship disorder, the Lord's Supper, spiritual gifts, and the unity of Christ's body.

rows.title: Day 15
rows.raw: Paul places love at the center of spiritual maturity and then applies it to gathered worship.

rows.title: Day 16
rows.raw: Paul defends the resurrection, then closes with practical instructions and affection for fellow workers.

rows.title: Day 17
rows.raw: Paul begins with the God of all comfort, explains affliction, and urges restored love toward a repentant offender.

rows.title: Day 18
rows.raw: Paul contrasts old and new covenant ministry and describes weakness as the setting for God's surpassing power.

rows.title: Day 19
rows.raw: Paul speaks of resurrection hope, pleasing Christ, new creation, reconciliation, and faithful ministry under hardship.

rows.title: Day 20
rows.raw: Paul rejoices over repentance and then points to the Macedonians' generous giving by God's grace.

rows.title: Day 21
rows.raw: Paul continues teaching about generosity, then defends ministry with spiritual rather than worldly weapons.

rows.title: Day 22
rows.raw: Paul warns against false apostles and describes boasting only in weakness because Christ's grace is sufficient.

rows.title: Day 23
rows.raw: Paul closes 2 Corinthians with a call to self-examination, then opens Galatians defending the one true gospel.

rows.title: Day 24
rows.raw: Paul defends justification by faith and confronts any return to law-based acceptance before God.

rows.title: Day 25
rows.raw: Paul describes adoption in Christ and calls believers to stand firm in freedom and walk by the Spirit.

rows.title: Day 26
rows.raw: Galatians closes with cross-shaped boasting, and Ephesians opens with praise for every spiritual blessing in Christ.

rows.title: Day 27
rows.raw: Paul explains salvation by grace and the mystery of Jews and Gentiles made one in Christ.

rows.title: Day 28
rows.raw: Paul moves from doctrine to the church's shared life, calling believers to unity, maturity, holiness, love, and light.

rows.title: Day 29
rows.raw: Ephesians ends with spiritual warfare and prayer, while Philippians begins with gospel partnership and courage.

rows.title: Day 30
rows.raw: Paul points to Christ's humility and exaltation, then counts everything loss because of the surpassing worth of knowing Him.

rows.title: Day 31
rows.raw: Philippians closes with peace, contentment, and generosity, while Colossians opens with the supremacy of Christ.

rows.title: Day 32
rows.raw: Paul warns against empty teaching and calls believers to live from their union with Christ.

rows.title: Day 33
rows.raw: Colossians closes with prayerful, gracious speech, and 1 Thessalonians opens by celebrating faith, love, and hope.

rows.title: Day 34
rows.raw: Paul recalls his gentle, honest ministry among the Thessalonians and his concern for their endurance.

rows.title: Day 35
rows.raw: Paul teaches about holiness, brotherly love, resurrection hope, the day of the Lord, and life together.

rows.title: Day 36
rows.raw: Paul comforts suffering believers and corrects confusion about the day of the Lord.

rows.title: Day 37
rows.raw: Paul calls for prayer, ordered work, and perseverance, then opens 1 Timothy by celebrating mercy to sinners.

rows.title: Day 38
rows.raw: Paul gives instructions about prayer, godliness, and qualifications for overseers and deacons.

rows.title: Day 39
rows.raw: Paul warns against false teaching, urges Timothy toward godliness, and gives practical care instructions for the church.

rows.title: Day 40
rows.raw: Paul warns about greed and calls Timothy to fight the good fight, then urges him not to be ashamed of the gospel.

rows.title: Day 41
rows.raw: Paul calls Timothy to endure as a faithful worker and continue in the Scriptures that make one wise for salvation.

rows.title: Day 42
rows.raw: Paul charges Timothy to preach the Word and finishes with personal reflections, while Titus is told to appoint qualified elders.

rows.title: Day 43
rows.raw: Paul describes sound teaching across generations and explains that God's grace trains believers for godly living.

rows.title: Day 44
rows.raw: Paul calls believers to gentle public conduct and grounds salvation in God's mercy, not works.

rows.title: Day 45
rows.raw: Paul appeals to Philemon to receive Onesimus no longer merely as a slave, but as a beloved brother.

rows.title: David anointed
rows.raw: Samuel is sent to Bethlehem to anoint the king God has chosen from Jesse's sons.

rows.title: David and Goliath
rows.raw: David faces Goliath while Israel's army is afraid and Saul's armor does not fit him.

rows.title: David and Saul
rows.raw: David succeeds, Jonathan loves him, and Saul grows jealous and afraid.

rows.title: Mercy in the cave
rows.raw: David has an opportunity to kill Saul, but he refuses to seize the throne by violence.

rows.title: David becomes king
rows.raw: David is made king over Israel, and the people name his call to shepherd and lead them.

rows.title: Worship and the ark
rows.raw: David brings the ark toward Jerusalem, and the chapter holds together holy reverence and public joy.

rows.title: God's promise
rows.raw: David wants to build a house for the Lord, but God promises to build David's house instead.

rows.title: David's sin
rows.raw: David remains in Jerusalem, takes Bathsheba, and arranges Uriah's death to cover his sin.

rows.title: Nathan confronts David
rows.raw: Nathan confronts David with a parable, and David is brought to confession.

rows.title: Repentance
rows.raw: Psalm 51 gives David's prayer of repentance after Nathan confronts him about Bathsheba.

rows.title: The shepherd king
rows.raw: David, once a shepherd and later king, prays of the Lord as his Shepherd.

rows.title: David's final charge
rows.raw: Near death, David charges Solomon to walk faithfully before the Lord as king.

rows.title: Moses preserved
rows.raw: Moses is born under Pharaoh's threat, hidden by faith, drawn from the water, and later flees after killing an Egyptian.

rows.title: The burning bush
rows.raw: At the burning bush, the Lord reveals His holiness, His name, His compassion, and His call for Moses.

rows.title: Passover
rows.raw: The Passover marks Israel's deliverance from judgment and slavery through the blood of the lamb.

rows.title: Through the sea
rows.raw: Israel is trapped between Pharaoh's army and the sea, and the Lord delivers them through the waters.

rows.title: Manna
rows.raw: Israel grumbles in the wilderness, and the Lord provides manna day by day.

rows.title: At Sinai
rows.raw: At Sinai, God reminds Israel of deliverance and calls them to covenant faithfulness.

rows.title: The commandments
rows.raw: God gives the Ten Commandments after declaring that He brought Israel out of slavery.

rows.title: The golden calf
rows.raw: While Moses is on the mountain, Israel makes the golden calf and worships what their hands have made.

rows.title: God's presence
rows.raw: After Israel's sin, Moses pleads for God's presence to go with His people.

rows.title: Spies in the land
rows.raw: The spies see the land's fruitfulness and its dangers, but most interpret the future through fear.

rows.title: Water from the rock
rows.raw: The people quarrel for water, and Moses strikes the rock instead of speaking to it as the Lord commanded.

rows.title: Moses' final view
rows.raw: Moses sees the land from a distance, dies, and is remembered as the prophet whom the Lord knew face to face.

rows.plan: 14 Days on the Life of Jesus
rows.title: Luke 2
rows.raw: Luke places Jesus' birth in ordinary history: a census, Bethlehem, a manger, and shepherds keeping watch.

rows.plan: 14 Days on the Life of Jesus
rows.title: Matthew 3
rows.raw: Jesus comes to John at the Jordan, where people are confessing sin and being baptized.

rows.plan: 14 Days on the Life of Jesus
rows.title: Matthew 4
rows.raw: After His baptism, Jesus is led by the Spirit into the wilderness and tempted by the devil.

rows.plan: 14 Days on the Life of Jesus
rows.title: Matthew 5
rows.raw: Matthew 5 begins the Sermon on the Mount, where Jesus teaches His disciples the character of kingdom life.

rows.plan: 14 Days on the Life of Jesus
rows.title: Mark 2
rows.raw: Mark gathers scenes where Jesus forgives, heals, calls Levi, eats with sinners, and teaches about Sabbath mercy.

rows.plan: 14 Days on the Life of Jesus
rows.title: Luke 15
rows.raw: Jesus tells these parables in response to grumbling that He welcomes sinners and eats with them.

rows.plan: 14 Days on the Life of Jesus
rows.title: John 6
rows.raw: After feeding the crowd, Jesus teaches that the sign points beyond bread to Himself.

rows.plan: 14 Days on the Life of Jesus
rows.title: John 10
rows.raw: Jesus uses shepherd imagery to describe His relationship to His sheep and His coming death.

rows.plan: 14 Days on the Life of Jesus
rows.title: John 11
rows.raw: Lazarus has died, and Jesus meets Martha and Mary in grief before going to the tomb.

rows.plan: 14 Days on the Life of Jesus
rows.title: John 13
rows.raw: During the last supper, Jesus washes His disciples' feet before teaching them to love one another.

rows.plan: 14 Days on the Life of Jesus
rows.title: John 17
rows.raw: Before the cross, Jesus prays to the Father for His disciples and for those who will believe through their word.

rows.plan: 14 Days on the Life of Jesus
rows.title: Matthew 26
rows.raw: Matthew 26 moves through betrayal, Passover, Gethsemane, arrest, and denial.

rows.plan: 14 Days on the Life of Jesus
rows.title: John 19
rows.raw: John records Jesus' trial, crucifixion, death, and burial with repeated attention to Scripture being fulfilled.

rows.plan: 14 Days on the Life of Jesus
rows.title: John 20
rows.raw: John 20 moves from the empty tomb to Jesus appearing to Mary, the disciples, and Thomas.

rows.title: Trust and wait
rows.raw: Psalm 37 teaches God's people how to respond when the wicked seem to prosper and outcomes feel delayed.

rows.title: Great faith
rows.raw: A centurion comes to Jesus for his servant, recognizing Jesus' authority even from a distance.

rows.title: Help my unbelief
rows.raw: A desperate father brings his son to Jesus after years of suffering and mixed hope.

rows.title: Faith credited
rows.raw: Paul reflects on Abraham's faith to show that righteousness is counted by grace, not achieved by works.

rows.title: Justified by faith
rows.raw: Paul describes the results of being justified by faith: peace, access, hope, endurance, and God's poured-out love.

rows.title: Live by faith
rows.raw: Paul explains life in Christ as crucified with Christ and now lived by faith in the Son of God.

rows.title: Saved by grace
rows.raw: Paul makes the order clear: salvation is God's gracious gift, and good works flow from His workmanship.

rows.title: Do not shrink back
rows.raw: Hebrews encourages weary believers to endure because God's promise is sure and the coming One will come.

rows.title: Faith made visible
rows.raw: James challenges empty claims of faith that do not become mercy toward people in need.

rows.title: Faith through trials
rows.raw: Peter blesses God for new birth into living hope while acknowledging grief in various trials.

rows.title: How long, O Lord
rows.raw: Psalm 13 is a short lament where David brings repeated 'How long?' questions before the Lord.

rows.title: The Shepherd's comfort
rows.raw: Psalm 23 traces the Shepherd's care through rest, restoration, guidance, danger, provision, mercy, and home.

rows.title: Near the brokenhearted
rows.raw: Psalm 34 names affliction, brokenheartedness, and the Lord's nearness and rescue.

rows.title: Hope in God
rows.raw: Psalm 42 speaks to a downcast soul while remembering God and longing for renewed praise.

rows.title: God is refuge
rows.raw: Psalm 46 names trouble, fear, shaking, and nations in uproar, yet confesses God as refuge and present help.

rows.title: God is my portion
rows.raw: Psalm 73 moves from confusion and envy into renewed nearness to God.

rows.title: Strength renewed
rows.raw: Isaiah speaks to weary people who wonder if their way is hidden from the Lord.

rows.title: I have called you by name
rows.raw: The Lord comforts His people with redemption, belonging, and promised presence through waters and fire.

rows.title: Mercies each morning
rows.raw: Lamentations remembers affliction and bitterness, then turns toward God's steadfast love, mercy, and faithfulness.

rows.title: Blessed are those who mourn
rows.raw: Jesus opens the Sermon on the Mount by announcing kingdom blessing to the poor in spirit, mourners, the meek, and others.

rows.title: Jesus wept
rows.raw: At Lazarus' tomb, Jesus meets grief with tears, prayer, authority, and resurrection power.

rows.title: Future glory
rows.raw: Paul places present suffering within the larger hope of creation's renewal and the redemption to come.

rows.title: God of all comfort
rows.raw: Paul praises the Father of mercies and God of all comfort in the middle of affliction.

rows.title: Every tear wiped away
rows.raw: Revelation 21 looks to new creation, God dwelling with His people, and the end of death, mourning, crying, and pain.

rows.title: Palm Sunday
rows.raw: Jesus enters Jerusalem as crowds shout Hosanna, then He enters the temple and confronts fruitless religion.

rows.title: Questions and teaching
rows.raw: Religious leaders test Jesus with questions, and He answers with wisdom about kingdom invitation, allegiance, resurrection, and the greatest commandment.

rows.title: Gethsemane
rows.raw: Matthew 26 moves through betrayal, Passover, Gethsemane, arrest, and denial.

rows.title: Servant love
rows.raw: During the last supper, Jesus washes His disciples' feet before teaching them to love one another.

rows.title: Jesus prays
rows.raw: Before the cross, Jesus prays to the Father for His disciples and for those who will believe through their word.

rows.title: The cross
rows.raw: John records Jesus' trial, crucifixion, death, and burial with repeated attention to Scripture being fulfilled.

rows.title: The resurrection
rows.raw: John 20 moves from the empty tomb to Jesus appearing to Mary, the disciples, and Thomas.

rows.title: Genesis 3
rows.raw: Human rebellion brings shame, judgment, and exile, yet God speaks a promise of defeat for the serpent.

rows.title: Genesis 12
rows.raw: God calls Abram and promises land, descendants, blessing, and blessing for all families of the earth.

rows.title: Isaiah 7
rows.raw: In a time of political fear, Isaiah gives the sign of Immanuel: God with us.

rows.title: Isaiah 9
rows.raw: Isaiah promises light for people in darkness and a child whose government and peace will not end.

rows.title: Isaiah 11
rows.raw: Isaiah looks for a shoot from Jesse's line, filled with the Spirit and ruling with righteousness.

rows.title: Micah 5
rows.raw: Micah promises a ruler from Bethlehem whose origins are ancient and whose greatness reaches to the ends of the earth.

rows.title: Luke 1
rows.raw: Luke 1 announces the births of John and Jesus, and Mary praises God for remembering His mercy.

rows.title: Luke 2
rows.raw: Luke places Jesus' birth in ordinary history: a census, Bethlehem, a manger, and shepherds keeping watch.

rows.title: Matthew 1
rows.raw: Matthew traces Jesus' genealogy and records the angel's word to Joseph about Mary's child.

rows.title: Matthew 2
rows.raw: Magi seek Jesus, Herod resists Him, and God protects the child through warning and flight.

rows.title: John 1
rows.raw: John begins before creation and announces that the eternal Word became flesh and dwelt among us.

rows.title: Galatians 4
rows.raw: Paul explains that God sent His Son to redeem those under the law so they might receive adoption.

rows.title: Philippians 2
rows.raw: Paul calls believers to humility by pointing to Christ's descent, obedience, death, and exaltation.

rows.title: Revelation 22
rows.raw: The Bible ends with the river of life, the tree of life, and the promise that Jesus is coming soon.

rows.title: Isaiah 53
rows.raw: Isaiah speaks of the suffering Servant who bears sin, is pierced, and yet sees life beyond His suffering.

rows.title: Matthew 28
rows.raw: Women come to the tomb, hear the angel's announcement, meet the risen Jesus, and receive a commission.

rows.title: Mark 16
rows.raw: The women come to anoint Jesus and find the stone rolled away and the tomb empty.

rows.title: Luke 24
rows.raw: Luke 24 moves from the empty tomb to the Emmaus road and Jesus opening the Scriptures to His disciples.

rows.title: John 20
rows.raw: John 20 moves from the empty tomb to Jesus appearing to Mary, the disciples, and Thomas.

rows.title: John 21
rows.raw: The risen Jesus meets His disciples by the sea, provides breakfast, and restores Peter.

rows.title: Acts 2
rows.raw: At Pentecost, Peter proclaims that God raised Jesus and made Him both Lord and Christ.

rows.title: Acts 4
rows.raw: Peter and John testify before leaders after healing a man in Jesus' name.

rows.title: Romans 6
rows.raw: Paul explains that believers are united with Christ in His death and resurrection.

rows.title: Romans 8
rows.raw: Romans 8 describes life in Christ, the Spirit's work, present suffering, future glory, and God's inseparable love.

rows.title: 1 Corinthians 15
rows.raw: Paul defends the resurrection and explains why Christ's resurrection is central to Christian hope.

rows.title: 1 Peter 1
rows.raw: Peter writes to suffering believers and begins with praise for new birth through Jesus' resurrection.

rows.title: Revelation 1
rows.raw: John sees the risen and glorified Christ, who declares that He was dead and is alive forevermore.

rows.title: Revelation 21
rows.raw: John sees the new heaven and new earth, where God dwells with His people and makes all things new.

rows.title: Birth of Jesus
rows.raw: Luke places Jesus' birth in ordinary history: a census, Bethlehem, a manger, and shepherds keeping watch.

rows.title: Baptism of Jesus
rows.raw: Jesus comes to John at the Jordan, where people are confessing sin and being baptized.

rows.title: Temptation
rows.raw: After His baptism, Jesus is led by the Spirit into the wilderness and tempted by the devil.

rows.title: Kingdom teaching
rows.raw: Matthew 5 begins the Sermon on the Mount, where Jesus teaches His disciples the character of kingdom life.

rows.title: Authority and mercy
rows.raw: Mark gathers scenes where Jesus forgives, heals, calls Levi, eats with sinners, and teaches about Sabbath mercy.

rows.title: Lost and found
rows.raw: Jesus tells these parables in response to grumbling that He welcomes sinners and eats with them.

rows.title: Resurrection and life
rows.raw: Lazarus has died, and Jesus meets Martha and Mary in grief before going to the tomb.

rows.title: Servant love
rows.raw: During the last supper, Jesus washes His disciples' feet before teaching them to love one another.

rows.title: Jesus prays
rows.raw: Before the cross, Jesus prays to the Father for His disciples and for those who will believe through their word.

rows.title: Gethsemane
rows.raw: Matthew 26 moves through betrayal, Passover, Gethsemane, arrest, and denial.

rows.title: The cross
rows.raw: John records Jesus' trial, crucifixion, death, and burial with repeated attention to Scripture being fulfilled.

rows.title: The resurrection
rows.raw: John 20 moves from the empty tomb to Jesus appearing to Mary, the disciples, and Thomas.

rows.title: Genesis 1
rows.raw: Genesis opens the Bible with God creating by His word, ordering the world, and making humanity in His image.

rows.title: Genesis 12
rows.raw: God calls Abram and promises land, descendants, blessing, and blessing for all families of the earth.

rows.title: Exodus 12
rows.raw: The Passover marks Israel's deliverance from judgment and slavery through the blood of the lamb.

rows.title: Joshua 1
rows.raw: After Moses' death, Joshua is called to lead Israel into the land God promised.

rows.title: 1 Samuel 16
rows.raw: Samuel is sent to Bethlehem to anoint the king God has chosen from Jesse's sons.

rows.title: 2 Samuel 7
rows.raw: David wants to build a house for the Lord, but God promises to build David's house instead.

rows.title: Isaiah 53
rows.raw: Isaiah speaks of the suffering Servant who bears sin, is pierced, and yet sees life beyond His suffering.

rows.title: Luke 2
rows.raw: Luke places Jesus' birth in ordinary history: a census, Bethlehem, a manger, and shepherds keeping watch.

rows.title: John 19
rows.raw: John records Jesus' trial, crucifixion, death, and burial with repeated attention to Scripture being fulfilled.

rows.title: Acts 2
rows.raw: At Pentecost, Peter proclaims that God raised Jesus and made Him both Lord and Christ.

rows.title: Romans 8
rows.raw: Romans 8 describes life in Christ, the Spirit's work, present suffering, future glory, and God's inseparable love.

rows.title: Revelation 21
rows.raw: John sees the new heaven and new earth, where God dwells with His people and makes all things new.
